sections.Interpretation: Marked leucocytosis with absolute lymphocytosis is present, with lymphocytes forming about 82 percent of total white cells and an absolute lymphocyte count of approximately 39 x10^9/L. Haemoglobin is marginally below the reference range and the red cell indices are normocytic and normochromic, consistent with mild anaemia of uncertain cause. Platelet count is markedly reduced. In a 58-year-old man with small cervical lymph nodes, this pattern is suggestive of chronic lymphocytic leukaemia, but it requires confirmation. Peripheral blood smear review by a haematologist and flow cytometry immunophenotyping of the lymphocyte population are recommended to establish clonality and guide further assessment.

errors.description: The interpretation says the platelet count is markedly reduced; the count is 152, within the reference range.
errors.rationale: The interpretation must agree with the numbers.

errors.description: Neutrophils are given as 22 percent; the differential then adds up to 110 and does not fit the absolute neutrophil count.
errors.rationale: The differential must add up to 100 and each absolute count must follow from the percentage and the white cell count.
